gloss: just the other day; only recently

definitions.gloss: just the other day; only recently; not long ago
definitions.explanation: An emphatic way of saying 'the other day,' stressing that the event happened very recently — typically within the last few days or weeks.

examples.japanese: つい{先日|せんじつ}{会|あ}ったばかりだ。
examples.english: I just saw them the other day.

examples.japanese: つい{先日|せんじつ}、{新|あたら}しいレストランがオープンした。
examples.english: Just the other day, a new restaurant opened.

examples.japanese: つい{先日|せんじつ}{買|か}ったばかりのスマホを{落|お}として{画面|がめん}が{割|わ}れてしまった。
examples.english: I dropped the smartphone I had just bought the other day and cracked the screen.

notes:
つい adds emphasis to {先日|せんじつ} (the other day), making it feel more immediate — 'just' the other day. The つい here conveys the sense of 'only just' or 'so recently that it still feels fresh.'

COMMON PATTERNS:
- つい{先日|せんじつ}～ばかり — just the other day (with ばかり for further emphasis)
- つい{先日|せんじつ}のことだ — it was just the other day

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {先日|せんじつ} — the other day (without the 'just' emphasis)
- つい{最近|さいきん} — just recently
- つい{昨日|きのう} — just yesterday
- この{間|あいだ} — the other day, recently (more casual)
